lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach Krameria as the hemiparasitic sister lineage with showy petaloid sepals, two oil-secretory petals, poricidal anthers and a spiny one-seeded fruit.

project_scope.selection_mode: Krameria erecta + Krameria lanceolata project module
project_scope.note: Krameriaceae is monogeneric, containing Krameria. Both project species are accepted and native in Texas.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: First recognize a low herb/shrub with alternate simple densely hairy leaves, then inspect the unusual zygomorphic flower. The showy pink/purple structures are largely sepals; two petals beside the ovary are modified into oil-secreting glands.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Green hemiparasitic herbs or shrubs; leaves alternate, usually simple, entire, exstipulate and densely strigose/tomentose. Haustoria attach to roots of nearby host plants.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers bisexual and zygomorphic. Five showy petaloid sepals surround five strongly modified petals; two petals function as oil glands. Stamens usually 4 with anthers opening by pores. Ovary superior and hairy.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Dry one-seeded capsule/fruit, globose to heart-shaped, usually armed with spines bearing retrorse/recurved barbs.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Hairy dryland plant + bizarre pink/purple flower with oil-gland petals + poricidal anthers + barbed one-seeded fruit = Krameriaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: hairy hemiparasitic habit → showy sepals vs petals → oil-gland petals → poricidal anthers → barbed fruit → species split
visual_lesson.intro: Krameriaceae is one of those families where learning what each flower part actually is completely changes what you see.

steps.title: 1 · Realize the showy parts are mainly sepals
steps.look_for: Five bright pink/purple petaloid sepals forming much of the visual display.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents misreading the flower as a conventional 5-petal bloom.

steps.title: 2 · Find the two oil-secreting petals
steps.look_for: Two small specialized petals beside the ovary with oil-filled blisterlike secretory tissue.
steps.why_it_matters: These modified petals are an exceptionally distinctive family trait.

steps.title: 3 · Look at the poricidal anthers
steps.look_for: Anthers release pollen through pores rather than long slits.
steps.why_it_matters: This helps explain the specialized bee interaction and reinforces the unusual floral architecture.

steps.title: 4 · Find the hidden hemiparasitism
steps.look_for: Green plants photosynthesize but also form root haustoria on neighboring hosts.
steps.why_it_matters: The family’s ecology is invisible above ground unless explicitly taught.

steps.title: 5 · Follow the ovary into the barbed one-seeded fruit
steps.look_for: Dry round/heart-shaped fruit armed with spines whose tips carry backward-pointing barbs.
steps.why_it_matters: Fruit is a very strong family confirmation.

steps.title: 6 · K. erecta vs K. lanceolata
steps.look_for: K. erecta is an upright shrub with solitary axillary flowers; K. lanceolata is spreading/decumbent with terminal one-sided racemes.
steps.why_it_matters: A simple architecture split helps route both project species.

comparisons.title: Krameriaceae vs Zygophyllaceae
comparisons.rule: Krameriaceae is hemiparasitic and zygomorphic with petaloid sepals, oil-secreting petals, poricidal anthers and a one-seeded spiny fruit; Zygophyllaceae project members are mostly radial and have multi-part capsules/schizocarps.

comparisons.title: Krameriaceae vs Fabaceae
comparisons.rule: Krameria can suggest a legume, but lacks stipules/legume fruit; its 4 poricidal stamens, oil-petal system and spiny one-seeded fruit are different.

comparisons.title: Krameriaceae vs Polygalaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can have zygomorphic flowers, but Krameria has the unique pair of secretory oil petals and poricidal anthers plus a barbed one-seeded fruit.

visual_lesson.caveat: Hemiparasitism is not visible from the shoot alone. Do not dig plants just to prove host attachment; use the floral/fruit characters in the field.

genera.fast_cue: hairy green hemiparasite + petaloid sepals + 2 oil-gland petals + poricidal anthers + barbed one-seeded fruit

visual_targets.annotation_goal: label 5 sepals and modified petals separately

visual_targets.structure: K. erecta vs K. lanceolata habit
visual_targets.annotation_goal: upright axillary vs spreading terminal-raceme architecture
